newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian elections postponed until June 15.
newsitem.headline: Haitian elections postponed until June 15.

text.p: Haitian election officials, under pressure from the international community, said on Thursday they had postponed a runoff election for seven seats in the nation's Senate until June 15.
The vote was to have taken place on Sunday.

"There was a lot of discussions, and we decided it was best not to hold the elections on Sunday," Provisional Electoral Council General Secretary Alexandre Lavaud told Reuters on Thursday. "There was also a last minute problem of organising the materials."
Diplomatic sources said the United Nations had stopped delivering ballots throughout the country last weekend, and negotiations to postpone the runoff ensued all week.
Officials said the United Nations, the United States and other countries close to Haiti were concerned about the political direction in which the elections were moving.

The seven seats up for grabs in the voting -- a runoff made necessary after the first round on April 6 -- were considered essential to control of the 27-member Senate, and its support for a plan to privatise state-run Haitian industries.
Haiti's Senate, the upper chamber of its Parliament which was dominated by the ruling Lavalas Political Organisation (OPL), only narrowly passed a U.S.-backed privatisation plan late last year.
Members of the international community have said they are concerned that narrow margin could slip away if the OPL loses many seats in the second-round vote.

The two Senate seats decided in voting on April 6 both went to former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide's Fanmi Lavalas party, which opposed privatisation. Fanmi Lavalas candidates seemed headed for victory in the second vote as well, in spite of complaints by OPL candidates of irregularities and election fraud.
Lavaud said the extra time was needed to investigate and correct any such irregularities.
